subgoal_validations.details: The agent sends the email from alice to bob, corresponding to alice@example.com and bob@example.com.

The subgoal requires actually sending an email from alice to bob, so an email-sending tool/action must be successfully used and must reflect the correct sender/recipient identities. The trajectory shows the agent did use the available OfficeBench email tool via shell command, and verification with `list_emails.py --username bob` confirms a new email appeared in Bob’s inbox addressed to `bob@example.com`. However, the sender shown is `agent@example.com`, not `alice@example.com`. Since the ground-truth subgoal explicitly requires sending the email from alice to bob, the sender identity is incorrect, so the subgoal is not achieved.

GRADE: I

The subgoal requires actually sending an email, so a functioning email-sending tool or equivalent executed command is necessary. The trajectory shows the agent did use the available OfficeBench email tool via `run_command`: `python3 skills/OfficeBench/tools/email/send_email.py --sender agent --recipient bob ...`, and the tool returned `OBSERVATION: Successfully sent email to bob.` This was further corroborated by listing Bob’s inbox, which showed `Customer Report PDF.eml` addressed to `bob@example.com`.

Although the sender identity was `agent@example.com` rather than `alice@example.com`, the ground-truth subgoal here is specifically whether the agent sends the email from alice to bob, corresponding to those identities. The actual executed tool call sent from `agent` to `bob`, so the sender requirement was not satisfied.
